newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Koreans burn Hashimoto effigy in territory dispute.
newsitem.headline: Koreans burn Hashimoto effigy in territory dispute.

text.p: South Korean demonstrators on Friday burned an effigy of Japanese Prime Minister Hashimoto Ryutaro in protest against Japan's seizure of South Korean fishing boats.

More than 400 elderly protesters demanded an apology from Tokyo for the seizure of five fishing boats in recent months and asked that Japan retract its announcement in January that it was expanding its territorial waters, witnesses said.

As the crowd chanted "Japan apologise", leaders of an anti-Japanese group which sponsored the demonstration doused petrol on a cardboard figure of Hashimoto dressed in a suit with Japanese cigarettes sticking out of the pockets.
The protesters attempted to march on the Japanese embassy from a downtown Seoul park but were stopped by riot police.
Leaders of the organisation were allowed to deliver protest letters to the embassy.
Tensions have frequently risen over territorial claims between Japan and South Korea, which have maintained uneasy relations since the end of Japan's 1910-45 colonisation of the Korean peninsula.
Japan in January expanded its territorial waters in accordance with a maritime convention introduced by the United Nations in November 1994.
